newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel says capacity will be cut to 1/3.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says capacity will be cut to 1/3.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, the Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator, said on Tuesday that its traffic will be cut to one third of normal levels after a fire swept through one of its main tunnels earlier, but it has given no timeframe for the reduced level of services.

A spokesman for Eurotunnel in London told Reuters: "We will operate at one third of normal capacity and we will give priority to Eurostar (express passenger) trains. But there will still be space for shuttle trains as well."
He did not say how many Eurostar or Le Shuttle trains would be cancelled as a result.
The Tunnel's operations have been closed after a fire engulfed part of one of the tunnels, near to the Calais end.
A Eurotunnel spokesman said the company did not yet know the full extent of damage to rolling stock or the tunnel or how much it could cost.

"It's quite messy down there. There will be damage to the overhead powerline cables, the heat will have buckled the steel rails and the carriages involved would be very badly damaged and may need to be replaced," he said.
The cost of a new train is 25 million pounds ($41.88 million), but Eurotunnel said it did not think an entire train would need replacing.
But added to the cost of possibly repairing tunnel and rolling stock damage will be possible compensation and paying for customers to travel by alternative methods such as air or ferry.
